decision.trend: Research has been focused on understanding the temperature-dependent plastic deformation behaviors of various high-entropy alloys (HEAs), with a trend towards investigating the effects of different processing routes, alloy compositions, and testing conditions on the mechanical properties and deformation mechanisms of these alloys. The studies have shown that HEAs can exhibit unique properties, such as high strength, ductility, and resistance to wear and corrosion, making them promising candidates for high-temperature applications.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in understanding the properties and behaviors of HEAs, there are still several unsolved questions and challenges, such as the development of a fundamental understanding of the relationships between alloy composition, processing, and properties, and the need for more systematic and comprehensive studies on the temperature-dependent deformation behaviors of HEAs. Additionally, the effects of chemical short-range order (SRO) on the mobility of dislocations and the resulting mechanical properties of HEAs are not yet fully understood.
decision.why: To further understand the temperature-dependent plastic deformation behaviors of HEAs, it is necessary to conduct in-situ experiments that can provide real-time observations of the microstructural evolution and dislocation dynamics during deformation at elevated temperatures. High-temperature in-situ TEM is a powerful tool that can provide such insights, enabling the direct observation of dislocation motion, grain boundary interactions, and phase transformations, which can help to elucidate the underlying mechanisms controlling the mechanical properties of HEAs.
